user_input: My ad says 'F₹€€ Shipping!!' and it got disapproved. What's wrong with it?
ideal_response: Your ad was disapproved under Google Ads Editorial Policy ADS-EDT-001. The issue is the use of gimmicky symbols and non-standard characters — specifically the currency symbols used to spell out 'FREE' and the repeated exclamation marks. Google requires ad text to use clear, standard language and formatting. To fix this, replace 'F₹€€ Shipping!!' with 'Free Shipping' or 'Free Delivery' — plain language, no special characters. Once you update the headline, resubmit the ad for review.

user_input: I wrote 'Buy great products here at low prices' for my new campaign headline and my ad keeps getting rejected. I don't understand why.
ideal_response: Your ad is being disapproved because the headline is too generic. Google Ads Editorial Policy ADS-EDT-001 requires that ad text be specific and relevant to what you're actually selling — phrases like 'Buy great products here' don't tell users what the product is, and Google treats this as a violation of editorial standards. To fix this, replace the headline with something specific to your product. For example, if you sell running shoes: 'Shop Men's Running Shoes — Free Returns' or 'Premium Trail Shoes Starting at $49'. The more specific your headline, the more likely it is to pass review.

user_input: My ad was approved last week but now it's showing as disapproved and I haven't changed anything in my campaign.
ideal_response: When an ad is approved and then later disapproved without any changes from your side, the most common cause is a change on the destination — your landing page. Google continuously checks that ad destinations are functional and accessible. I'd recommend checking the following: First, open the landing page URL in a private browser window to confirm the page is loading correctly. Second, check that your site isn't returning a 404 or 500 error. Third, verify that the display URL in your ad still accurately reflects the actual landing page URL. If all of those look fine and your ad is still disapproved, there may be a technical issue — I can escalate this to a human support agent for deeper investigation.
escalation_condition: Advertiser confirms site is live and URL is correct

user_input: My competitor's ads are running just fine but mine keep getting rejected. My landing page looks totally normal to me. What else could be causing this?
ideal_response: One issue that is easy to miss is the browser back button. Google Ads Destination Policy ADS-EDT-001 requires that landing pages allow users to navigate back freely using the browser's back button. Some landing page builders or JavaScript pop-up scripts disable this by pushing multiple history states, which traps users on the page. To check for this: open your landing page in Chrome, click anywhere on the page, then try pressing the browser back button. If the page reloads instead of going back, or if a pop-up appears that prevents navigation, that is likely the cause of your disapproval. You'll need to remove or adjust the script causing this behavior.

user_input: We're targeting Spanish speakers in the US but our ads are written in English. Is that allowed under Google's policies?
ideal_response: Under Google Ads Technical Requirements (ADS-EDT-001), your ad content and destination content must match the language you are targeting. If your campaign is set to target Spanish-language users, your ads and landing page should be in Spanish, or at minimum contain the primary language of your target audience. Running English-language ads against a Spanish-language targeting setting is a technical violation and your ads may be disapproved or underperform significantly. To resolve this, either update your ad copy and landing page to Spanish, or change your targeting language setting to English if your audience is English-speaking.

user_input: My HTML5 banner ad displays correctly on desktop but appears completely blank on mobile devices. What's going on?
ideal_response: This is a technical issue covered under Google Ads Technical Requirements (ADS-EDT-001). HTML5 ads must function correctly across all supported environments — an ad that appears blank on mobile does not meet this requirement and may be disapproved from mobile placements. There are a few common causes: the ad may be using JavaScript APIs not supported on mobile browsers, the animation may rely on features blocked by Safari or Chrome on iOS, or the fallback image may be missing. Because diagnosing HTML5 rendering issues requires inspecting the ad code and environment logs, I'm going to connect you with a technical support specialist who can investigate this directly.
